basis: Inherited skin fragility and blistering; enamel hypoplasia affects teeth in 30-79%. Oral mucosal blistering alone is below 30%.
Sarcoma arising predominantly in deep soft tissues of the limbs and trunk; no other organ consistently involved.
Inherited high myopia, documented in 15/15 patients.
Mesenchymal tumor arising within the central nervous system, usually the supratentorial brain.
Nonsyndromic congenital fusion of digits; a structural limb malformation.
Inflammation of subcutaneous fat; the umbrella includes diverse causes and does not establish a uniform immune-mediated mechanism.
Skeletal dysplasia characterized by abnormal pelvic development.
Congenitally shortened small intestine with malrotation; metabolic acidosis reported in 3/3 patients supports common acid-base dysfunction.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia/respiratory failure common, profound intellectual disability 80-99%, hearing impairment 30-79%; redundant skin lacks functional damage.
Immune-mediated inflammation of the corneal stroma, often triggered by infection, with potential corneal scarring and visual loss.
Clonal hematopoietic neoplasm involving myeloid and sometimes lymphoid lineages; lymphoma is not universal across presentations.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia with severe ossification defects; lung hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and contributes to neonatal death.
Eye-origin lymphoma; direct CNS involvement develops in roughly 60-80% of the predominant primary vitreoretinal form during its course.
Progressive renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis and tubular loss; anemia is secondary to kidney failure, and extrarenal ciliopathy features are a minority.
Congenital nephrosis and ocular malformations define the syndrome; developmental impairment occurs in 30-79%, with motor delay and microcephaly in 3/4.
Intestinal smooth-muscle dysfunction with megaduodenum in 6/6; urinary retention in 1/6 and unspecified bladder findings do not establish the 30% threshold.
Intellectual disability and epilepsy accompany defining hypogonadism and diabetes; autoimmune causation of the syndromic diabetes is not established.
Peroxisomal disorder; severe brain dysfunction, hepatobiliary disease and retinal/optic damage each commonly exceed 30%; renal dysplasia omitted because of the cap.
Defining spastic paraplegia and intellectual disability, ocular dysfunction with nystagmus and refractive abnormalities, and obesity in 3/4 patients.
Benign familial brain overgrowth, also termed megalencephaly; head enlargement does not establish additional organ damage.
Congenital urethral obstruction affecting the urinary tract; pulmonary hypoplasia is below 30%, and recurrent urinary infections are separate diagnoses.
Deficient pituitary hormone secretion; additional structural or neurologic disease depends on the underlying subtype.
Solitary benign cutaneous histiocytic proliferation; the definition does not describe systemic histiocytosis or blood involvement.
Autoimmune neuromuscular junction dysfunction causing limb-girdle weakness; ocular weakness is junctional, and associated autoimmune diseases are separate.
Vascular insufficiency of the spinal cord, potentially progressing to spinal cord infarction.
